results.title: An Introduction to Stochastic Volatility Jump Models - Kidbrooke Blog
results.content: # An Introduction to Stochastic Volatility Jump Models. Stochastic Volatility Jump Diffusion (SVJD) is a type of model commonly used for equity returns that includes both stochastic volatility and jumps. The advantage of the model is that it is possible to replicate stylized facts such as heavy tails and volatility clustering and mean reversion, negative correlation between returns and volatility, and sudden large movements in the price of the asset. Here, as an example, we present the basic case of a combination of Merton's jump diffusion model and Heston's stochastic volatility model. Merton's model is based on the classic Black-Scholes model but extended to include discontinuous asset returns. The stochastic volatility in Heston's model is a mean-reverting square-root process. $$ \begin{align} \frac{dS\_t}{S\_t} &= \mu\_t\,dt + \sqrt{\eta\_t}\,dW\_t^{(1)} + (J\_t-1)\,dq\_t \label{eqn:level\_sde} \\ d\eta\_t &= \kappa(\theta - \eta\_t)\,dt + \sigma \sqrt{\eta\_t}\, dW\_t^{(2)} \label{eqn:variance\_sde} \end{align}$$. The variance process \(\eta\_t\), Equation \(\ref{eqn:variance\_sde}\), is mean reverting with mean reversion level \(\theta\), mean reversion strength \(\kappa\) and constant volatility \(\sigma\).

results.content:
Title: Statistical properties and economic implications of jump-diffusion processes with shot-noise effects - ScienceDirect
The shot-noise jump-diffusion (SNJD) model aims to reflect how economic variables respond to the arrival of sudden information. ► This article studies the shot-noise jump-diffusion model (SNJD). This article focuses on a continuous-time process named shot-noise jump-diffusion (SNJD, hereafter) model, recently proposed by Altmann et al. This process enlarges the Jump-Diffusion (JD) models introduced by Merton (1976) by adding a new term called shot-noise function. The shot-noise function attenuates the effect of abrupt changes (*jumps*) in economic variables, an issue not correctly modeled by JD processes. The structure of this paper is as follows: Section 2 presents a general treatment of the shot-noise process and the SNJD model. This section introduces the shot-noise process and the SNJD model, presenting some of their main features. This article has focused on the shot-noise jump-diffusion (SNJD) model posited by Altmann et al. The SNJD process extends traditional jump-diffusion (JD) models by adding a shot-noise function to the Poisson term, trying to reflect how economic variables respond to the arrival of sudden information. ### Modeling Greek equity prices using jump diffusion processes. (2011) study the shot-noise jump diffusion model and their empirical study indicates that 73% of extreme risks may cause autocorrelation effects. Bates [20] added jump ingredients to asset prices to improve the Heston model, where a jump is a compound Poisson process following a normal distribution. Given that the traditional Black–Scholes (BS) model is difficult to adapt to ever-changing financial markets, to better describe real financial markets, this paper presents a generalized European option-pricing model with stochastic volatility and stochastic interest rates and pure jumps under Levy processes, which are stochastic processes with both stationary and independent increments. And various stock price processes with jump components have been proposed in the past literature, such as pure jump process by Cox and Ross (1976), jump diffusion process by Merton (1976) and Kou and Wang (2004), and jump diffusion process with short noise by Altmann et al. Different from most of the current studies in equilibrium pricing under jump diffusion models, this work models the underlying asset price as the exponential of a Lévy process and thus allows nearly an arbitrage distribution of the jump component.
